angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 379,852 km at 43.98 pc = 0.12 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 22.7374 +/- 0.0220 mas (same row, RUWE 1.06): 43.98 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.546 +/- 0.018 solar radii from Diamond-Lowe et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-3 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....164..172D/abstract): 379,852 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.549 +/- 0.029 solar masses from Diamond-Lowe et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-3 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....164..172D/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3844 +/- 61 K from Diamond-Lowe et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-3 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....164..172D/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Diamond-Lowe et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-3 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....164..172D/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-3.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.703, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
